title: Mersenne achievement set: greedy geometry, fat-Cantor structure, and the 1/2 membership question

concepts.label: Mersenne weight w(n)=1/(2^n-1) and its tail T(n)
concepts.description: The summand of Erdos #257 and the total mass strictly after exponent n (GreedyAchievementSet.lean:56,95).

concepts.label: strict superincreasing tail T(n) < w(n)
concepts.description: The Kakeya-type condition making the achievement set a Cantor set rather than an interval.

concepts.label: Mersenne achievement set M
concepts.description: All real values of sum over A of 1/(2^a-1) over normalized supports A (0 not in A); range of the binary digit map (GreedyAchievementSet.lean:571).

concepts.label: the target value 1/2
concepts.description: Whether 1/2 lies in M is the whole open question of this zone; a yes answer refutes universal Erdos #257.

concepts.label: fat Cantor structure
concepts.description: M is compact, perfect, totally disconnected and nowhere dense yet has Lebesgue measure exactly one.

concepts.label: finite cylinder stage
concepts.description: Nested compact depth-d enclosures whose intersection is M and whose measure is 2^d * T(d).

concepts.label: greedy residual orbit r_n(x)
concepts.description: Take exponent n+1 iff w(n+1) <= r_n; the canonical selection whose survival characterises membership.

concepts.label: skipped support of the greedy orbit
concepts.description: The exponents the greedy run declines; for x=1/2 its infinitude is equivalent to membership.

concepts.label: gap g(n) = w(n) - T(n)
concepts.description: The positive slack at rank n; asymptotically (2/3)4^-n + O(8^-n).

concepts.label: two-channel decomposition of w(n)
concepts.description: w(n) = 2^-n + 4^-n + remainder, with remainder controlled by 8^-n; the source of every explicit constant in the zone.

concepts.label: correction tail eta_m
concepts.description: T(m) minus its dyadic channel 2^-m; pinned strictly inside (2^-(2m+2), 2^-(2m+1)).

concepts.label: skip caps (dyadic and two-channel)
concepts.description: Sufficient upper bounds on the residual at a skipped rank that would force perpetual survival.

concepts.label: signed balance 2 r_n - T(n)
concepts.description: Signed distance of the residual from the midpoint of the remaining tail; drives the one-step survival criterion.

concepts.label: greedy shadow
concepts.description: Prefix mass plus complementary tail, whose distance to the Erdos-Borwein constant equals the signed balance.

concepts.label: Erdos-Borwein constant T(0)
concepts.description: Sum of all 1/(2^n-1); irrational (Erdos 1948), which is what excludes the lazy boundary case.

concepts.label: straddle prefix
concepts.description: A finite exponent word u with W(u) <= t <= W(u) + T(d); the cut-locator coordinate for the target t.

concepts.label: fatal rank gap
concepts.description: A finite prefix whose next-rank window strictly brackets the target, excluding every support extending it.

concepts.label: integer half carry K_N
concepts.description: Affine binary orbit K_0 = 1, K_{N+1} = 2 K_N - a_{N+2}; equals 2^{N+1}(1/2 - series) plus a bounded tail.

concepts.label: square-root strip 1 <= K_n <= 2*sqrt(n)+4
concepts.description: The finite search window inside which half-carry words are looked for.

concepts.label: strip-admissible finite half word
concepts.description: A finite Boolean word all of whose prefix carries stay in the strip; prefix-closed, hence Konig-compact.

concepts.label: even half-divisor seam
concepts.description: The unresolved transition at an even depth, whose scalar model reaches every terminal carry except the single hole 2*delta-c.

concepts.label: Mobius-centred half carry
concepts.description: K_N recentred by the signed Mobius baseline so that its coboundary is exactly the support bit minus the divisor sum.

concepts.label: integer-greedy seam word
concepts.description: Row-indexed finite integer words whose achievement values approximate 1/2 from below.

concepts.label: last greedy skip M
concepts.description: A final skipped exponent; its existence is equivalent to 1/2 not being in M.

concepts.label: producer socket
concepts.description: A named unproved Prop packaged so that assuming it yields 1/2 in M; the dominant shape in this zone.

concepts.label: post-take unsafe band
concepts.description: The rational interval in which the last skip of a run fails the dyadic safety test.

concepts.label: reverse carry word
concepts.description: Bit/coefficient/carry triple with bit + 2*carry = coeff + next carry, used for 2-adic spacing of overlapping returns.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For every positive exponent n the Mersenne weight 1/(2^n-1) strictly exceeds the total remaining mass of all later weights, and that remaining mass is at most twice the next weight and tends to zero. This strict superincreasing property is what makes the value set a Cantor-type set instead of an interval.
statement_nodes.engine: term-by-term geometric domination w(n+j) <= w(n)*2^-j
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The strict-tail (Kakeya) criterion for subsum sets is classical; for this exact Mersenne family the Cantor geometry is recorded by Kovac-Tao, and docs/claims.json makes no novelty claim.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Each Mersenne weight splits exactly as 2^-n + 4^-n plus a positive remainder bounded by 2*8^-n, so the tail splits as 2^-n + (1/3)4^-n plus a remainder tail lying strictly between (1/7)8^-n and (2/7)8^-n. Consequently the gap w(n) - T(n) equals (2/3)4^-n up to an error of norm at most 3*8^-n, and is big-O of 8^-n at infinity.
statement_nodes.engine: geometric expansion of 1/(2^n-1) as sum over j>=1 of 2^-jn, then summing the tail channelwise
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Elementary geometric-series bookkeeping; the value of the node is the explicit constants that every later separation estimate consumes.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The Mersenne support value of a set of positive exponents coincides with the generic erdosSupportSeries at base 2, the achievement set is exactly the range of the continuous binary digit map, and that map is injective, so distinct normalized supports have distinct values.
statement_nodes.engine: uniform normed-series convergence for continuity; strict superincreasing tail for injectivity
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Injectivity of a superincreasing binary coding is the standard Cantor-coding argument; index zero is normalised away because its analytic weight is zero.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The Mersenne achievement set is compact, closed, perfect, totally disconnected and nowhere dense in the reals.
statement_nodes.engine: topological embedding of the Cantor cube via the digit map, plus bit-flip perturbation for perfection
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Kovac-Tao record the Cantor geometry of this exact strict-tail family; the ledger entry greedy_achievement_geometry is explicitly labelled 'formalised here' with no novelty claim.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The depth-d cylinder stage is a disjoint union of 2^d translated copies of an interval of length T(d), hence has Lebesgue measure exactly 2^d * T(d); the stages are nested with intersection equal to the achievement set, and 2^d * T(d) tends to 1. Therefore the achievement set has Lebesgue measure exactly one while being nowhere dense: it is a fat Cantor set.
statement_nodes.engine: exact disjoint-split volume recursion plus continuity of measure from above on a nested compact family
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Measure-one-yet-nowhere-dense subsum sets are classical (Kakeya/Guthrie-Nymann circle of results); the Mersenne instance is attributed to Kovac-Tao in the ledger.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: A real x lies in the Mersenne achievement set if and only if x is nonnegative and the greedy residual after every finite number of steps is at most the remaining tail. Moreover the greedy run applied to the value of a normalized support recovers exactly that support, and the greedy residual at level n equals the suffix value of the support.
statement_nodes.engine: superincreasing greedy inversion: survival forces the residual to zero, and the selected support reproduces x
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Standard greedy-representation theory for superincreasing sequences. Both sides are decidable-in-the-limit statements about a given x; neither side is the open problem for general x.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For rational inputs the exact rational greedy recursion takes a term at rank n+1 exactly when the real greedy recursion does, the rational prefix is the audited finite Erdos sum of the selected exponents, and for a rational value already known to be in the achievement set the membership bits of its support are computed by the rational greedy test. So the digits of a rational achievement point are decidable at every finite depth.
statement_nodes.engine: cast commutation between the rational and real recursions
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Exactness plumbing so that finite computations are kernel-checked rather than floating point.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: If at some level the greedy residual strictly exceeds the remaining tail then the point is not in the achievement set; and a purely rational certificate, comparing an exact rational upper enclosure of the tail with the exact rational residual, soundly implies the same nonmembership. The certificate is one-sided: failing to find one, or surviving to any finite depth, proves nothing about membership.
statement_nodes.engine: finite-lookahead rational tail enclosure T(n) < prefix + upper bound of remaining geometric mass
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Immediate contrapositive of the survival characterisation; the content is decidability, not mathematics.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The value 3/4 is not in the Mersenne achievement set, certified by a level-one death certificate with zero lookahead.
statement_nodes.engine: exact rational evaluation of the level-one residual against the level-one tail enclosure
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: A single decidable certificate check; it says nothing about the 1/2 question.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Once the greedy run at some level has residual strictly above the remaining tail, that condition persists and every later exponent is taken, so the skipped support is finite. Contrapositively, for any nonnegative x whose greedy run skips infinitely many exponents, x belongs to the achievement set.
statement_nodes.engine: monotone propagation of the fatal inequality through the greedy step
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Direct consequence of the survival characterisation and the strict superincreasing tail.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The value 1/2 belongs to the Mersenne achievement set if and only if the canonical greedy run started at 1/2 skips infinitely many exponents. Both sides of this equivalence are open: nothing in the corpus decides either.
open_antecedents: (greedyMersenneSkippedSupport (1 / 2 : R)).Infinite -- equivalently (1 / 2 : R) in mersenneAchievementSet; neither is proved anywhere in the corpus
statement_nodes.engine: Erdos-Borwein irrationality on the finite-skip branch, plus the fatal-level propagation
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: This is the pivot equivalence of the zone. Every 'iff' theorem in Z12 whose right-hand side is one of these two conditions is a restatement of the same open question in different coordinates.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: No finite normalized set of positive exponents has Mersenne support value 1/2, and no finite support value plus a full tail equals 1/2 either. Hence if 1/2 is in the achievement set the witnessing support is automatically infinite, and its existence would refute universal Erdos #257.
statement_nodes.engine: odd reduced denominators of finite Mersenne sums for the greedy endpoint; Erdos-Borwein irrationality for the lazy endpoint
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The denominator-parity argument is elementary; the lazy endpoint imports the classical irrationality of the Erdos-Borwein constant.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The Erdos-Borwein constant, the sum of 1/(2^n-1) over all positive n, is irrational; it is also the total tail mass T(0), and it splits as the greedy support value plus the skipped support value for any starting point.
statement_nodes.engine: imported irrationality result of the corpus
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Erdos 1948 (and Borwein); formalisation only.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: If at every rank the greedy run started at 1/2 has residual at most the two-channel cap 2^-(n+1) + (1/3)4^-(n+1) whenever it skips that rank, then 1/2 belongs to the Mersenne achievement set; the same holds with the smaller dyadic cap 2^-(n+1). Neither skip-branch cap hypothesis is proved anywhere.
open_antecedents: hskip : forall n, not (mersenneWeight (n+1) <= greedyMersenneRemainder (1/2) n) -> greedyMersenneRemainder (1/2) n <= halfTwoChannelCap (n+1)
hskip : forall n, not (mersenneWeight (n+1) <= greedyMersenneRemainder (1/2) n) -> greedyMersenneRemainder (1/2) n <= halfDyadicCap (n+1)
statement_nodes.engine: cap induction: selected branches transport the cap for free because the cap decreases by less than one weight
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The proved content is only the induction skeleton; the arithmetic burden sits entirely on the unproved skip-branch hypothesis.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For every positive m the correction tail (the Mersenne tail minus its dyadic channel) is pinned strictly between 2^-(2m+2) and 2^-(2m+1), so the sharp uniform window depth is 2m+1, and the rank gap decomposes exactly as (w(n) - 2^-n) minus the correction tail at n.
statement_nodes.engine: two-channel bounds (1/3)4^-m plus remainder tail in ((1/7)8^-m, (2/7)8^-m)
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: A sharp but elementary consequence of the channel bounds already established.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The forced-return threshold at (m, J) equals T(m) minus the correction tail at m+J; a residual r satisfies r minus the next J Mersenne weights at most 2^-(m+J) exactly when r is at most that threshold. The threshold is strictly increasing in J with limit T(m), so any residual strictly below T(m) forcibly returns under the dyadic cap after finitely many blocks, and any residual at most the two-channel cap returns after at most about m/2 blocks.
statement_nodes.engine: strict monotonicity of the threshold in the block length plus convergence to the tail
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Genuine unconditional bookkeeping about the block structure of returns; it constrains no actual orbit by itself.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: In the rational sliver coordinate a selected greedy step acts by the exact affine map x maps to (4 + 2/(2^n-1))x - 1, and in the doubled sharp coordinate by 4x - 2 plus a 2/(2^n-1) correction. So the greedy dynamics on the sliver is an explicitly perturbed times-four map.
statement_nodes.engine: direct rational algebra
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: A change of coordinate on the greedy step; no orbit statement follows from it here.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Two exact rational fixtures at rank three: r = 37/280 lies in the relaxed escape window with sliver coordinate 2/5 and survives a further undoubled step, while r = 67/512 has sharp sliver coordinate 21/32 yet already exceeds the Mersenne tail at rank three. Together they show that the relaxed and doubled two-thirds tests are not equivalent to actual survival.
statement_nodes.engine: exact rational evaluation
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Regression fixtures guarding against an over-strong reading of the band tests.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For the greedy run at 1/2 the correction interval at depth n is contained in the complementary dyadic cell exactly when the residual lies between the correction tail and 2^-n, and that two-sided condition is exactly the bound |signed balance| <= 2^-n minus the correction tail.
statement_nodes.engine: interval containment unfolded into two inequalities
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Coordinate identity; neither side is proved to hold for the actual orbit at any rank beyond the checked fixtures.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Given that the greedy residual survives at level n, the next level survives if and only if the rank gap g(n+1) is at most the absolute signed balance at n; and when it does survive, the new absolute signed balance is |(old absolute balance) - w(n+1)|. This is an exact one-step dynamical law for the survival question.
statement_nodes.engine: case split on the take/skip branch of the greedy step
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Exact reformulation of the survival step; it converts the open problem into an open statement about a one-dimensional folding map, without solving it.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The greedy shadow at depth n minus the Erdos-Borwein constant equals the signed balance, so one-step survival at 1/2 is equivalent to the rank gap being at most the distance from the shadow to that constant; moreover any competing prefix separated from the greedy prefix by more than the tail is strictly further from the constant.
statement_nodes.engine: prefix-plus-tail splitting of the Erdos-Borwein constant
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Same content as the signed-balance criterion in shadow coordinates; a dress change, useful only if a shadow-side estimate ever appears.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: If for every positive n the second-channel phase 4^n * (residual at 1/2) stays at distance at least 1/6 + (37/56)2^-n from 1/3, then 1/2 belongs to the Mersenne achievement set; equivalently it suffices that the decidable rational separation predicate holds for every n at least 7. The separation hypothesis is not proved for any n beyond the checked range.
open_antecedents: hseparate : forall n, 0 < n -> (1/6 : R) + (37/56) * (1/2)^n <= |greedyMersenneSecondChannelPhase n - 1/3|
hseparate : forall n, 7 <= n -> HalfSecondChannelSeparatedRat n
statement_nodes.engine: 4^n scaling of the signed balance identity, plus the uniform bound 4^n * g(n+1) <= 1/6 + (3/8)2^-n
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: This is a hole-avoidance socket: it asks the rescaled orbit to avoid a shrinking interval around 1/3 forever. No mechanism for that is supplied.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The decidable rational second-channel separation predicate holds at every rank n with 1 <= n <= 6, checked by exact rational arithmetic.
statement_nodes.engine: decidable rational comparison
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Bounded check only; the socket needs all n >= 7 and nothing here extends past 6.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: A normalized support has Mersenne value exactly 1/2 if and only if its correction value (the Mersenne minus dyadic discrepancy over the support) equals its complement value (the dyadic mass of the complementary exponents beyond one). Both sides are open for any candidate support.
open_antecedents: halfCorrectionValue A = halfComplementValue A for some normalized A -- equivalent to positiveMersenneSupportValue A = 1/2, i.e. the open half-membership question
statement_nodes.engine: subtracting the dyadic geometric series 1/2 = sum of 2^-n over n >= 2 term by term
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: An exact rearrangement of the target equation; it moves the difficulty rather than reducing it.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: If a normalized support carries a prefix forcing chain -- correction and complement values trapped in a common family of dyadic cells whose depths tend to infinity -- then the two values coincide and 1/2 belongs to the Mersenne achievement set. No such chain is constructed anywhere in the corpus.
open_antecedents: chain : HalfPrefixForcingChain A -- existence of a normalized A whose correction and complement values are trapped in dyadic cells of unbounded depth
statement_nodes.engine: analytic coinduction: two points in a common cell of depth d differ by at most 2^-d
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The structure field bundles the whole difficulty; the theorem is the trivial limit step once a chain is granted.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: An interval of length at most one contains at most one integer, so at most one dyadic rational of depth 2m+1 can lie inside a correction window of width the correction tail at m; combined with the exact cancellation of powers of two in dyadic boundaries this pins the crossing depth.
statement_nodes.engine: scaling the window by 2^(2m+1) and applying integer uniqueness
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Elementary; supplied as reusable plumbing for the cut locator.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Exact rational facts about the actual greedy orbit at 1/2 and its correction tail: 1/2 minus the Mersenne sum over {2,3,6,7} is 1/16002; over {2,3,6,7,14} it is 1/688086; the correction tail at 1 is at most 5/42 and 3/8 < 1/2 minus it; exponent 2 is taken and exponent 4 is skipped by the greedy run at 1/2.
statement_nodes.engine: exact rational evaluation and finite tail enclosure
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Bounded-depth checks. In particular the skipped support at 1/2 is known nonempty (4 is in it) but nothing here shows it infinite.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: A finite exponent word straddles a target t at depth d when its Mersenne value is at most t and t is at most that value plus the tail at d. If straddling words exist at every depth then t belongs to the Mersenne achievement set -- compactness replaces any nested-chain or coinductive interface. A straddling word at depth d either still straddles at d+1, or straddles after adjoining d+1, or exposes a fatal rank gap; straddles also restrict downward by erasing the top exponent.
statement_nodes.engine: compactness of the achievement set plus a finite-word trichotomy at each rank
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: A genuine criterion for arbitrary targets. It becomes the open question only when specialised to t = 1/2.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For the target 1/2 both straddle boundary equalities are impossible, so every half straddle is strict; the rank step is the strict dichotomy 'refine or expose a fatal gap'; and any half-straddling finite word agrees with the actual greedy support at 1/2 on all ranks up to its depth. The cut-locator coordinate is therefore canonical, not branch-dependent.
statement_nodes.engine: odd reduced denominators of finite Mersenne sums and Erdos-Borwein irrationality to kill the two boundary cases
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: This canonicality is what upgrades a branch-local gap into a global exclusion; it is the load-bearing lemma of the cut locator.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: If a target t sits strictly above a support prefix plus the tail after rank d+1 and strictly below that prefix plus the weight at d+1, then no support agreeing with the prefix through rank d can have value t. The exclusion is global over supports, not merely about the greedy branch.
statement_nodes.engine: split the support value at rank d and bound the suffix by the tail
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Elementary but the correct scoping statement: it is what makes a single finite witness decisive.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Either 1/2 belongs to the Mersenne achievement set or some finite exponent word exhibits a fatal half gap, and these alternatives are exclusive: the existence of a fatal half gap is logically equivalent to 1/2 not belonging to the achievement set. Which branch holds is exactly the open question; the corpus decides neither.
open_antecedents: ExistsFatalHalfGap -- equivalently (1/2 : R) not in mersenneAchievementSet; neither branch is proved
statement_nodes.engine: straddle canonicality plus the global rank-gap exclusion, driven by compactness
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: A clean reformulation into a search problem over finite words: a single fatal witness would settle nonmembership. It is still a restatement of the open question, and the module says so.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The empty word straddles the target 1/2 at depths 0 and 1, so the cut-locator search is nonvacuous at its base.
statement_nodes.engine: exact rational evaluation of the tails at depth 0 and 1
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Base case only.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For a residual written as 1/R after a take at rank b with q = 2^b - 1, and next take at rank c with m = 2^(c-1), the last intervening skip fails the dyadic safety test exactly when R lies strictly in (q(m-1)/(q+m-1), qm/(q+m)), an interval of exact width q^2/((q+m)(q+m-1)). For a single intervening skip this is the two-thirds band, of width below 1/9 and contained in (2q/3, 2q/3 + 2/9), where an unsafe skip forces 2q < 3R < 2q + 2/3.
statement_nodes.engine: rational algebra on the post-take reciprocal R*q/(q-R)
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Elementary and self-contained. Two limitations are stated by the module itself: dyadic safety is strictly stronger than what the greedy run needs, and the single-skip specialisation is only one of the run lengths that actually occur at 1/2.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: An integral reciprocal never lies in the two-thirds band, because the pinning 2q < 3R < 2q + 2/3 leaves no room for a multiple of three. For a residual p/(2D) in lowest terms with p, D and q all odd, an unsafe single-skip run forces p >= 7: the band defect 6D - 2pq is divisible by four, and that congruence alone removes p in {1,3,5}.
statement_nodes.engine: 2-adic congruence on the band defect
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Local constraints on one take-skip-take step. No theorem here says that the actual greedy orbit at 1/2 avoids a band, so this is not a step towards either branch of the half question.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The integer half carry K_N (K_0 = 1, K_{N+1} = 2K_N minus the support coefficient at N+2) satisfies the exact identity K_N = 2^(N+1)(1/2 minus the support series) plus the binary coefficient tail at N+1, and depends only on the support below level N+1, so it is unchanged by restricting or by inserting exponents at least two levels ahead.
statement_nodes.engine: affine binary orbit unfolding against the divisor-coefficient sequence
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: A change of coordinates: smallness of the scaled carry is exactly closeness of the support series to 1/2.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Finite Boolean half words, their supports, and strip admissibility (bits 0 and 1 false, and every prefix carry inside 1 <= K <= 2*sqrt(n)+4) form a prefix-closed system: admissibility is preserved by restriction to shorter words. Terminal reachability and full-strip reachability at a level are the derived search predicates.
statement_nodes.engine: locality of the integer half carry under restriction
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Functoriality plumbing; it is exactly what a Konig argument needs.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Every integer has a unique fixed-coefficient parent, and under a half-divisor coefficient change at parent delta the reachable terminal carries are exactly all integers other than the single value 2*delta - c. Inside a bounded strip this becomes: k is reachable iff k lies in the strip and k is not 2*delta - c. Uniqueness of the parent persists when the parent is required to lie inside the previous strip.
statement_nodes.engine: parity inverse of k = 2h - c or 2h - c - 1; discharged by integer case analysis
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Exact and elementary. It converts a reachability question into the single arithmetic question of where the hole 2*delta - c sits relative to the strip; it does not answer that question.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: At the scalar parameters delta = 2, c = 1 the terminal carry 3 is not even-seam reachable, so the hole can genuinely fall inside the strip at small depth.
statement_nodes.engine: direct arithmetic
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: A single negative instance; it is the reason the seam-escape hypothesis is needed rather than provable at low depth.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: With numerators tracked, even-seam reachability splits into exactly two sheets: below the hole the numerator is 2T - c - 1 - k, above it 2T - c - k. Hence when the hole lies below the strip the whole strip recylindrifies on the upper sheet, and when it lies above the strip the whole strip recylindrifies on the lower sheet.
statement_nodes.engine: case split on k relative to 2*delta - c
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Refinement of the one-hole theorem carrying the numerator coordinate; still purely scalar.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: A family of predicates on finite Boolean words that is closed under restriction and nonempty at every length admits an infinite Boolean sequence all of whose finite restrictions satisfy it; specialised, cofinally many strip-admissible finite words give an infinite strip-admissible branch.
statement_nodes.engine: Konig's lemma over the finitely branching tree of finite Boolean words
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Konig's lemma; formalisation only.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: IF an infinite Boolean branch all of whose finite prefixes are strip admissible exists, THEN its support omits 0 and 1, is infinite, and has support series exactly 1/2; so a single such branch would be a counterexample to universal Erdos #257. The Lean theorems take the branch as a free hypothesis (hbranch : forall N, HalfStripAdmissible N (a restricted to N)); no branch is constructed anywhere in the corpus.
statement_nodes.engine: the scaled-residual identity plus the subexponential strip envelope, forcing the residual to zero
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Unconditional given a branch. No branch is constructed; every route below is an attempt to supply one. Reclassified from unconditional_object_theorem on adversarial review: the branch hypothesis is a free, never-discharged antecedent, the same shape as tempered_mobius_carry_yields_half (which is already conditional_implication), and the conclusion is the open target itself rather than a quantitative estimate.
open_antecedents: hbranch : forall N : Nat, HalfStripAdmissible N (fun i => a i) -- existence of even one infinite strip-admissible Boolean branch. Nothing in the corpus produces one: exists_infinite_halfStripBranch (HalfCarryReachability.lean:429) needs hfinite : forall N, exists a : HalfWord N, HalfStripAdmissible N a, which is exactly the unproved HalfCarryCofinalAdmissibility of node cofinal_admissibility_yields_257_counterexample. If such a branch existed, universal Erdos #257 would be refuted, so the antecedent is at least as hard as the open problem.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: Conditional on an object of unknown existence. The theorem constrains no actual orbit: it says only what a strip-admissible branch would have to be worth, not that one exists. Contrast straddle_prefix_membership_criterion, whose hypothesis has known instances (e.g. t = 0, and the depth-0/depth-1 half straddles of initial_half_straddle_instances); the strip-admissible-branch hypothesis has none.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: If every terminal carry in the square-root strip is reachable by some strip-admissible finite word at every level (or at every level beyond some base level with an admissible base word), then there is an infinite set A with the sum of 1/(2^a-1) over A equal to 1/2. The full-strip reachability hypothesis is not proved at any level beyond finite search.
open_antecedents: hfull : forall N, 1 <= N -> HalfCarryFullStripReachabilityAt N
hfull : forall N, N0 <= N -> HalfCarryFullStripReachabilityAt N, together with hbase : exists a : HalfWord N0, HalfStripAdmissible N0 a
statement_nodes.engine: Konig compactness on strip-admissible words, then the branch-forces-half theorem
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: A producer socket. The conclusion would refute universal Erdos #257, which is itself a reason for scepticism about the antecedent being cheap.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Much less than full-strip reachability suffices: if strip-admissible finite words merely exist at cofinally many levels, then there is an infinite set A whose Mersenne sum is exactly 1/2. The cofinal-existence hypothesis is not proved.
open_antecedents: hcofinal : HalfCarryCofinalAdmissibility, i.e. forall N, exists M >= N and a : HalfWord M with HalfStripAdmissible M a
statement_nodes.engine: restriction closes the family downward, so cofinal nonemptiness gives nonemptiness at every level; then Konig
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Strictly weaker antecedent than full-strip reachability, so this is a genuine socket weakening rather than a restatement.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: If at every sufficiently large even depth the actual reachability set is described by a canonical scalar seam, and every such seam's hole escapes the strip, then full strip reachability holds at those even depths, cofinal admissibility follows, and hence an infinite set with Mersenne sum 1/2 exists. Adding an odd-level reachability hypothesis and a depth-20 admissible base word gives the same conclusion. Neither the seam-supply nor the seam-escape hypothesis is proved.
open_antecedents: hcanonical : HalfCarryCanonicalEvenSeamSupply, i.e. forall d >= 10, exists delta c, IsCanonicalEvenSeam d delta c
hescape : HalfCarryEvenSeamEscape, i.e. forall d >= 10 and every canonical seam, 2*delta - c < 1 or halfStripBound (2d) < 2*delta - c
hodd : forall d >= 10, HalfCarryFullStripReachabilityAt (2d+1)
hbase : exists a : HalfWord 20, HalfStripAdmissible 20 a
statement_nodes.engine: the exact one-hole theorem: a hole outside the strip restores full reachability
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The proved part is the one-hole bridge. The two named Props carry all remaining difficulty, and the depth-14 instance shows the hole can sit inside the strip at small depth.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The signed Mobius baseline has divisor sums equal to 0 at n = 1 and 1 at every other positive n.
statement_nodes.engine: Mobius inversion over the divisor lattice
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Standard Mobius inversion; formalisation only.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Recentring the integer half carry by the signed Mobius baseline gives a carry whose coboundary is exactly the support coefficient minus the divisor-sum baseline: a_{N+2} minus the divisor sum equals 2*C_N minus C_{N+1}.
statement_nodes.engine: affine recentring of the binary orbit
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: A change of variables presenting the half question as a coboundary equation; no new content on its own.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For the actual greedy run at 1/2 the Mobius-centred half carry is nonnegative at every level. This is the lower half of the square-root strip, proved unconditionally for the real orbit; only the upper bound remains open.
statement_nodes.engine: greedy underestimation (the greedy support series never exceeds the target) fed into the scaled-residual identity
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Genuine unconditional statement about the actual object, but it is a short consequence of greedy underestimation plus the carry identity, so it is probably a routine corollary rather than new mathematics.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: If the Mobius-centred half carry of a normalized support divided by 2^N tends to zero, then that support has Mersenne sum exactly 1/2 and is infinite; a pointwise bound by 2*sqrt(N)+4 is a sufficient concrete producer, and applied to the greedy support at 1/2 it would give a counterexample to universal Erdos #257. No such temperedness or square-root bound is proved.
open_antecedents: htempered : Tendsto (fun N => (mobiusCenteredHalfCarry A N : R) / 2^N) atTop (nhds 0)
hbound : forall N, (mobiusCenteredHalfCarry (greedyMersenneSupport (1/2)) N : R) <= 2 * sqrt N + 4
statement_nodes.engine: scaled-residual identity plus subexponential envelope
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The nonnegativity half of the strip is proved elsewhere in this zone; only the upper bound is missing, which is exactly the hard half.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: A normalized finite half word of depth M with terminal carry in the square-root strip has support series within (4M+12)/2^M of 1/2; more generally the distance is at most (absolute terminal carry plus 2*sqrt(M)+4) divided by 2^M. No coherence between depths and no bound on earlier carries is needed.
statement_nodes.engine: the scaled-residual identity with the universal binary coefficient tail bounded by the strip envelope
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Genuine and sharp enough to replace the inverse-system argument by closedness of the achievement set.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: If normalized finite words with terminal carry inside the square-root strip exist at cofinally many depths, then 1/2 belongs to the Mersenne achievement set and there is an infinite set with Mersenne sum 1/2. The cofinal terminal-witness supply is not proved.
open_antecedents: hcofinal : HalfCarryCofinalTerminalOnlyStrip, i.e. forall N, exists M >= max N 1 with a normalized HalfWord M whose terminal carry has absolute value at most halfStripBound M

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The square-root strip envelope divided by the binary place value tends to zero, both at index M and at the successor index M+1.
statement_nodes.engine: polynomial over exponential limit
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Standard limit; isolated so several consumers can share it.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: If there is a sequence of normalized finite half words with depths tending to infinity whose absolute terminal carries divided by 2^depth tend to zero, then 1/2 belongs to the Mersenne achievement set and an infinite set with Mersenne sum 1/2 exists. The square-root-strip cofinal supply maps into this weaker interface, so it is a genuine weakening rather than a parallel restatement; but no such sequence is constructed.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Each integer-greedy seam word codes a normalized finite exponent set, so its Mersenne value lies in the achievement set and equals the cast of an exact rational seam sum.
statement_nodes.engine: normalisation of the seam word support
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Bookkeeping so that a limit of seam values can be taken inside the closed set.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For every seam row s at least 5 the exact rational seam remainder is nonnegative and at most 2^-s plus the integer seam remainder divided by 4^s; equivalently the seam value approaches 1/2 from below with error at most 2^-s plus the normalized integer remainder.
statement_nodes.engine: exact floor identity for the integer seam remainder
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Unconditional but useless on its own: the error term is controlled only if the normalized integer remainder is small, which is exactly the open input.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: If along some sequence of rows tending to infinity the integer seam remainder divided by 4^s tends to zero, then the seam values converge to 1/2 and, by closedness, 1/2 belongs to the Mersenne achievement set. No such row sequence is exhibited.

statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Weakest of the seam sockets: cofinal and only subquadratic, rather than a uniform exponential bound.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: If the integer seam remainder is below 2^(s+1) for every row s at least 6 -- an exponential bound observed by exact replay but not proved -- then the seam values approach 1/2 with error at most 3*2^-s and 1/2 belongs to the Mersenne achievement set.

statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The antecedent is empirical extrapolation from replayed rows; the module labels it an honest socket and does not assert it.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Membership of 1/2 in the Mersenne achievement set is equivalent to each of: the integer seam not being eventually right-extending; false successor terminal bits occurring beyond every bound; such bits occurring along one cofinal sequence; some cofinal seam sequence with skipped ranks tending to infinity; infinitude of the skipped support of the real greedy half orbit; and the nonexistence of a last greedy skip. All of these are the same open statement in different coordinates.
open_antecedents: SeamGreedyUnboundedTerminalFalse -- equivalently (1/2 : R) in mersenneAchievementSet; no positive producer for any member of the ring is proved
statement_nodes.engine: Boolean complement of the fatal-gap/right-tail classification, transported through the seam-to-greedy dictionary
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The module states this itself: these are consumer equivalences that isolate the remaining arithmetic task without asserting any of the equivalent positive conditions. Counting them as six results would badly overstate progress; they are one restatement.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: At a fixed seam row at least 5, the successor terminal bit is false exactly when the row is in the upper-or-middle arithmetic case (the old successor carries to the upper word, or there is no carry and the new terminal weight exceeds the explicit prefix remainder); unbounded occurrence of the two conditions therefore coincide.
statement_nodes.engine: row-local case analysis of the integer seam step
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The row-local half (seamGreedy_terminal_false_iff_upperOrMiddle) is a genuinely local classifier: at any fixed row it is decidable, and it is unconditional finite-rank content. The global half (unboundedTerminalFalse_iff_unboundedUpperOrMiddle) is a change of vocabulary on the open problem and carries no new content.
open_antecedents: SeamGreedyUnboundedUpperOrMiddle -- and equally its partner SeamGreedyUnboundedTerminalFalse. By half_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_iff_unboundedTerminalFalse (HalfCylinderHalfMembershipClassification.lean:126) the latter is provably equivalent to (1 / 2 : R) in mersenneAchievementSet, so both sides of unboundedTerminalFalse_iff_unboundedUpperOrMiddle are open and neither has a positive producer anywhere in the corpus.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: Flagged as a restatement on adversarial review. The node bundles two statements of different status. seamGreedy_terminal_false_iff_upperOrMiddle (line 57) is per-row, decidable, and genuinely unconditional. unboundedTerminalFalse_iff_unboundedUpperOrMiddle (line 98) is an equivalence both of whose sides are equivalent to the open half-membership question, and belongs to the same restatement ring as half_membership_seam_equivalence_ring; it renames the open problem rather than reducing it. The restatement flag is set because of the second declaration only.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: If a family of rational-linear channels each annihilates every vector killed by scalar evaluation, and evaluation is surjective, then the evaluation matrix has rank at most one, so every square minor indexed by a type with at least two elements has determinant zero. This is an abstract linear-algebra fact about an arbitrary channel family satisfying the kernel hypothesis; read informally it says that a determinant route built from relation-invariant channels fails at every rank rather than only at the experimentally tested ranks two through four, but see the scope caveat for what the Lean does and does not instantiate.
statement_nodes.engine: rank-one factorisation of relation-invariant functionals (linearDescender_eq_smul_eval) plus vanishing of minors of a rank-one matrix
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: Rules out only determinant-based separation built from channels that annihilate the kernel of scalar evaluation, i.e. channels factoring through evaluation, and only for index types with at least two elements (Nontrivial iota); a single-channel 1x1 determinant is untouched. It does not rule out: channels that fail that invariance (any channel sensitive to a nontrivial zero-valued formal relation); nonlinear or non-rational channels; height or adelic obstructions established by means other than a nonvanishing minor; or the reverse-carry 2-adic spacing route in the same module. It says nothing about whether 1/2 is in the achievement set. IMPORTANT, added on adversarial review: the theorem is stated for an arbitrary V, ev and channel family, and no declaration anywhere in the corpus defines the concrete shifted channels used in the experiments or proves that they satisfy hker. So the reading 'this closes the raw shifted-channel determinant route' (module docstring, HalfTrappingReturnCarry.lean:11-15) is an informal application, not a formalised one; the formal content is the abstract rank-one minor vanishing. Any published claim that a method family is closed must either instantiate the channels in Lean or state the gap.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Standard linear algebra once the rank-one factorisation is available; the value is the scoping, namely that the failure is structural at all ranks rather than accidental at small ranks.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Two reverse-carry presentations that share a coefficient word, differ at a single 1/0 seam, and agree on the following overlap of length L have terminal carry difference equal to 2^L times an odd integer; if both terminal carries are nonnegative and bounded by a common real bound, then 2^L is at most that bound. Specialised to overlapping midpoint returns at depth 2N with seam at M, the exponent is 2N - M - 1.
statement_nodes.engine: doubling iteration of the carry difference across the overlap, with a single odd increment at the seam
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: True as stated, but currently without a consumer: the corpus supplies no reverse-carry presentation arising from a failed greedy separation and no earlier overlapping return, so the predecessor-supply obligation is unmet and no separation or irrationality claim follows.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Assuming a final skipped exponent M for the greedy run at 1/2, the finite Mersenne shift of the skipped prefix satisfies exact relations: 1/2 plus the shift minus the Erdos-Borwein constant equals the residual minus the tail at M, lies strictly in the one-sided fatal interval (0, g(M)), the centred shadow at M-1 is within g(M) of the constant, and for M at least 3 the constant minus the shift lies in the dyadic window (1/2 - 4^-M, 1/2).
open_antecedents: hlast : IsLastHalfGreedySkip M -- existence of a final skipped exponent, which is itself equivalent to (1/2 : R) not in mersenneAchievementSet and is not proved
statement_nodes.engine: exact prefix/tail splitting of the Erdos-Borwein constant under the last-skip hypothesis, plus the gap bound g(M) < 4^-M for M >= 3
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: These are consequences drawn under the negative branch, intended for a contradiction that is not reached. They are not restatements of the open problem, but they only bite once an external input contradicts the dyadic window.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Campbell's use of the Alford-Granville-Pomerance estimate fixes exponent 1/4, so at prime-search height P the progression modulus d must satisfy d^4 <= P. In the proposed last-skip synchronization the requirements 2 <= d, t <= d, P <= 4t and d^4 <= P are jointly inconsistent, and so is the phase-freeze variant with window inequality P*q0^2 <= 2M+2 and M <= t*q0^2. Hence that synchronization cannot be made to work at those parameters.
statement_nodes.engine: elementary integer inequality chain d^4 <= P <= 4t <= 4d forcing d < 2
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: Rules out only the specific parameter conjunction arising from the delta = 1/4 choice: 2 <= d, t <= d, P <= 4t, d^4 <= P (and its phase-freeze variant). It does not rule out a Campbell-style prime-progression input with a different exponent, a different window-to-period relation, a larger admissible modulus, or any other route to infinitely many greedy skips; and it does not touch the half-membership question itself.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The inequality is trivial; the content is the faithful transcription of Campbell's parameter requirements. This is precisely the kind of barrier that must be scoped tightly: it closes one parameter set, not a method family.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: A last greedy skip exists exactly when the skipped support of the greedy run at 1/2 is finite, and exactly when a fatal half gap exists. All three conditions are equivalent to 1/2 not lying in the Mersenne achievement set.

statement_nodes.prior_art_note: A dictionary between the cut-locator and the greedy coordinates; no new content beyond the pivot equivalence.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The proposed shifted-window interface -- under a putative last skip M at least 3, the Erdos-Borwein constant minus the finite skipped shift is at most 1/2 - 4^-M -- is logically equivalent to infinitude of the greedy skipped support at 1/2, and hence to 1/2 belonging to the Mersenne achievement set. It is therefore an endpoint restatement, not an independent producer: assuming it assumes the conclusion. Any future Campbell-style input must be nonvacuous, for example a window theorem without the last-skip guard.

Any socket in this zone whose antecedent is guarded by IsLastHalfGreedySkip deserves the same check.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For every support the uncentred integer half carry divided by 2^N is antitone in N, because each step subtracts a nonnegative support coefficient after rescaling.
statement_nodes.engine: one-line rescaling of the carry recursion
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Elementary monotonicity, but it is what turns a cofinal condition into a limit statement.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: If the actual greedy half carry returns to the square-root strip beyond every index, then antitonicity forces the whole scaled carry to zero, the greedy support at 1/2 is infinite with Mersenne sum exactly 1/2, and 1/2 belongs to the achievement set. The cofinal return hypothesis is not proved.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Strict superincreasingness of the Mersenne weights is hereditary: for any set J of future offsets and any positive n, the sum of the selected future weights is still strictly less than w(n). So every Mersenne subseries inherits the Cantor-type rigidity.
statement_nodes.engine: indicator domination against the full tail
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Immediate monotone comparison with the full-tail inequality; the generality over J is the only new element.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For any prescribed offset set J, the Mersenne digit map restricted to digit strings supported in J is injective, so distinct J-supported digit strings give distinct achievement values.
statement_nodes.engine: hereditary strict superincreasingness applied to the first differing digit
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Specialisation of the standard superincreasing-coding injectivity argument to a restricted support.
